title: CTCL Treatment by Stage
subtitle: Skin-directed, systemic, and chemotherapy options organized by TNMB stage

skin-directed.text: Superpotent topical corticosteroid · NB-UVB · PUVA · Topical mechlorethamine (gel or ointment) · Topical carmustine · Local radiation (4-6 Gy for symptomatic lesions)
skin-directed.detail: First-line standard: Skin-directed therapy is the mainstay for early-stage disease. Superpotent (class I) topical steroid for limited lesions. NB-UVB preferred for patch-stage; PUVA for thicker plaques or folliculotropic variant. Topical mechlorethamine (Valchlor gel) is FDA-approved. Local RT for isolated symptomatic lesions.

systemic-nochemo.text: Usually NOT indicated for Stage IA. For Stage IB with extensive disease or rapid progression: bexarotene oral or topical · Low-dose methotrexate · IFN-alpha
systemic-nochemo.detail: Systemic therapies reserved for skin-directed therapy failures in Stage IB. Bexarotene (rexinoid) 300 mg/m2/day; monitor triglycerides and thyroid. IFN-alpha 3 MU TIW subcutaneous. Low-dose methotrexate 5-25 mg weekly for refractory disease.

rows.name: Stage IIA-IIB (N+ nodes or T3 tumors)

skin-directed.text: Continue skin-directed therapy · Targeted radiation to tumors (8-36 Gy) · Total Skin Electron Beam Therapy (TSEBT) 12-36 Gy (low-dose 12 Gy preferred to reduce toxicity)
skin-directed.detail: Skin-directed therapy remains important even as systemic agents are added. TSEBT is effective for extensive plaque/tumor-stage disease; low-dose (12 Gy in 8 fractions) has comparable efficacy with less toxicity. Targeted RT (palliative) at 4-8 Gy for individual painful or ulcerated tumors.

systemic-nochemo.text: Bexarotene · IFN-alpha · Low-dose methotrexate · Mogamulizumab (CCR4 inhibitor) · Brentuximab vedotin if CD30 expression ≥10% · Romidepsin or vorinostat (HDAC inhibitors)
systemic-nochemo.detail: Stage IIB key additions: Mogamulizumab (anti-CCR4 mAb) showed superior PFS vs vorinostat in Phase III. Brentuximab vedotin (anti-CD30 antibody-drug conjugate) FDA-approved for CD30+ CTCL ≥10%; ORR ~50-60% in tumor-stage MF. Histone deacetylase inhibitors (romidepsin, vorinostat) are options for refractory disease.

chemo-sct.text: Reserved for refractory Stage IIB: gemcitabine (single-agent) · Liposomal doxorubicin · Clinical trial preferred
chemo-sct.detail: Single-agent chemotherapy for Stage IIB refractory to multiple systemic agents. Gemcitabine (1000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, 15 of 28-day cycle) has ORR ~50-60% but responses are not durable. Clinical trial enrollment strongly encouraged.

rows.name: Stage III / Erythrodermic MF / Sézary Syndrome

skin-directed.text: Low-potency topical steroids for symptom control · NB-UVB (if tolerated) · Avoid aggressive TSEBT unless isolated nodal disease
skin-directed.detail: Erythrodermic patients have compromised skin barrier; aggressive skin-directed therapy may worsen condition. Gentle emollient regimens, low-potency topical steroids, and NB-UVB for palliation. TSEBT occasionally used for symptom control.

systemic-nochemo.text: Extracorporeal Photopheresis (ECP) — first-line for erythrodermic/Sézary · Mogamulizumab · IFN-alpha · Bexarotene · Low-dose alemtuzumab (off-label) · Combination ECP + IFN or ECP + bexarotene
systemic-nochemo.detail: ECP cornerstone: Leukapheresis-based immunomodulatory therapy; ORR 30-80% for erythrodermic CTCL/SS. Combine with IFN-alpha or bexarotene for enhanced response. Mogamulizumab superior to vorinostat in randomized trial (MAVORIC) with ORR 28% vs 5% in SS. Alemtuzumab (anti-CD52) effective but immunosuppressive; monitor for CMV reactivation.

chemo-sct.text: Refractory Stage III/SS: gemcitabine · Liposomal doxorubicin · Pralatrexate · Consider allogeneic HSCT for younger fit patients with IVA2
chemo-sct.detail: Allogeneic HSCT offers potential long-term remission in Sézary syndrome refractory to multiple agents. Reduced-intensity conditioning preferred given older age at presentation. Graft-versus-lymphoma effect documented. Refer to transplant center early in refractory cases.

rows.name: Stage IV / Visceral or N3 Disease (IVA1, IVA2, IVB)

skin-directed.text: Palliative local radiation for symptomatic lesions · Gentle topical therapy for symptom control

systemic-nochemo.text: Mogamulizumab · Brentuximab vedotin (CD30+) · Romidepsin · Pralatrexate · Bexarotene + ECP (IVA2/SS) · Clinical trial strongly preferred
systemic-nochemo.detail: Systemic options palliative at Stage IV; durable remissions are rare without SCT. Mogamulizumab ORR ~28-37%. Pralatrexate (antifolate) ORR ~35%. Coordinate with multidisciplinary lymphoma team. Enroll in clinical trial whenever possible.

chemo-sct.text: Allogeneic HSCT (curative intent) · Gemcitabine-based regimens · CHOP or CHOP-like chemotherapy for rapidly progressive IVB · Liposomal doxorubicin
chemo-sct.detail: Allogeneic HSCT: Only potentially curative option for advanced CTCL. Best outcomes in patients achieving at least partial remission before transplant. Non-relapse mortality 15-30%; graft-versus-lymphoma effect documented. IVB with visceral disease: systemic chemotherapy (gemcitabine, liposomal doxorubicin) + radiation for bulky disease + referral for allogeneic HSCT if fit and chemosensitive.

skin-directed.text: Photo-document BSA at every visit · Repeat biopsy if transformation suspected

systemic-nochemo.text: CBC + Sézary count every 3-6 months · LDH · CT/PET if stage IIA or higher
systemic-nochemo.detail: Large-cell transformation (LCT) — emergence of >25% large cells (CD30+) — is a poor prognostic sign requiring repeat biopsy. LCT prognosis is poor with median OS <2 years; brentuximab vedotin is preferred systemic option for CD30+ LCT.

chemo-sct.text: Post-SCT: chimerism monitoring + GVHD surveillance every 3 months
